# Breadcrumb

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

navigation and disclosure · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

Shows where a page sits in the site. Real links, no JavaScript.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/docs', label: 'Docs' },
    { label: 'Breadcrumb' },
  ]}
/>
```

Leave `href` off the last item: it becomes the current page (`aria-current="page"`).
The items with an `href` are also written as `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD for search engines.

For Arabic, pass `labels={getLabels('ar').labels}`. It names the `<nav>`; the crumbs are your own text.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `items`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | **yes** | `readonly BreadcrumbItem[]` | - | The trail as `{ href?, label }`, root first. An item with an `href` is a link and joins the JSON-LD; the last one without is the current page. |
| `labels` | no | `Labels` | - | The built-in strings; the nav is named by `labels.breadcrumb.label`. Defaults to English. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
